status: LIVE design data v4: the vertical slice (milestones M1, M2a and M2b; survival_gdd.md version 4). The game and tests/survival/test_survival_data.gd read these rows. Every number is tunable.
summary: Livelihoods in the slice, measured in rv per game day whether the output is eaten, worn, kept, bartered or sold: living from the woods, making for trade, trapping and hunting; the firewood contract; labour jobs at the landing and for the mentors.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify
basis_keys.H: standard historiography (books in the GDD sources list); verify before quoting
basis_keys.H-regional: true for one region's trade or society (named in the row); not yet checked for New York
basis_keys.M: modern science or medicine sets the mechanic (period explanation may differ)
basis_keys.D: design value for balance, or a figure resting on web summaries; not a checked historical record

design.rule: The player lives mainly from the woods and trades surplus. Livelihoods are measured in rv per game day, whether the output is eaten, worn, kept, bartered or sold. Trapping in the winter, hunting in the fall and the garrison's firewood are still there, and the credit year for players who take a book.
design.unit: reference value (rv, economy.json reference_value) per game day; cash-equivalent pence where coin changes hands at the trader
design.ladder: Skilled trapping (24 traps) earns at least twice the best safe wage; novice trapping and novice hunting at least 0.8 of a common day wage (tested in cash-equivalent terms).

hunting_reference.rule: Deer come from the region's stock (map_regions.json fauna.deer), which recovers by animals drifting in from the wider manor lands; the garrison meat cap applies; half the meat is eaten or given away.

design.credit_year: Optional: Fall outfit on credit (Mid September) -> fall deerskins -> the trap line (November to March) -> the winter visits (payments) -> the spring settlement window (Mid April to Early May) sets next year's outfit.

livelihoods.name: Trapping
livelihoods.notes: Deadfalls and steel land sets in the manor woods; the trader's visits and the sutler buy. Winter beaver lodge hunts and water sets are backlog (M5): in the Albany and Great Lakes trade of the 1760s steel traps were being made by colonial smiths, so the lodge hunt is one real method among several, not 'the usual way' in New York (N:23 is H-regional for the Hudson's Bay lowlands; N:36).

livelihoods.name: Hunting for skins and meat
livelihoods.notes: Meat is mainly food and a gift; the cash product is the fall skin. The sutler's meat channel takes a little venison at one price, capped (the peace detachment buys a third of a wartime garrison's).

livelihoods.name: Living from the woods
livelihoods.notes: Food, clothing and stores made and kept. The M2a gate's T1 and T5 measure it with the self_sufficient policy.

livelihoods.name: Making for trade
livelihoods.notes: Moccasins and mitts to the soldiers while the sutler is sold out, buckskin to the farm family and the trader, snowshoes to the trader.

jobs.name: Cut the garrison's firewood
jobs.task: split wood (wood.split_firewood) and stack it at the fort woodpile: 18 d a cord, paid in coin at each cord stacked; or rations (4 lb flour and 1.5 lb salt pork a cord) [D]
jobs.risk: cuts (hurry doubles them), cold at the woodpile

jobs.name: Carry at the landing
jobs.task: carry the trader's goods up from the landing on the fall and spring visits: paid in goods, coin or book credit (7 d a game hour of rv)

jobs.name: Carry the sutler's stores
jobs.task: carry the fall and spring stores into her loft: pays in a lesson or a favour, not coin

jobs.name: Split the sutler's wood
jobs.task: split and stack her winter wood: pays in a lesson or a favour

jobs.name: A day on the old hunter's line
jobs.task: walk his line with him, carry and re-set: the work is the lesson

jobs.name: Cut the old hunter's wood
jobs.task: cut and carry his winter wood: pays in a lesson or a favour
